result.verdict: No, most viewers won't reach the end, though the film is on target rather than broken. The consensus curve holds 68% at 0:30 and 58% at 1:00 (both inside the playbook's targets) and averages about 35.7% AVD (6:01 of 16:51), right at the 35% target. About 16% are still there when the voice ends at 16:38 and about 10% at 16:51. The spread by audience is wide: 28% for a Shorts-trained 19-year-old, 42% for a geography fan. Viewers tire in three places. First, 1:40-2:55, a roll-call of people who noticed the pattern (Bacon recap, Forster's flood, Humboldt, the hook's list read again, two 1970s jokes), with nothing new on the 'why' since 0:31: the curve sheds 8 points in minute 2 and 5 in minute 3, and the casual viewer leaves at 2:41. Second, and milder, 4:35-5:20: six statistics at 172-178 wpm over near-still globes under a single 3-minute music bed, which is where the average viewer starts to tire. Third, and the one that costs the ending, everything after 'They're scars' (11:33). The proof itself is a 1.3-s blur. It is followed by a tangent (Nevada), an empty frame at 12:56, the stillest minute of the film (13:30-14:30) and a 30-s recap at 14:04 that sounds like the end, so the curve sags 2.1-2.4 points a minute just before the four-continents payoff and comment prompt promised at 0:47. Between those stretches, the pyramid, Wegener and Gondwana chapters (5:57-11:12) hold at about 1.5 points a minute. Fixes 1-11 are cuts, picture-only re-renders and audio edits with no new narration. They take about 1:17 out (to roughly 15:34) and should lift AVD to roughly 39-40% and end-screen reach to about 19-20%. Order of work: apply the re-renders and the vo_proc.wav cleanup first, then make every cut in one edl.py pass. All times in this plan are on the current 16:51 master.

fixes.problem: 1:39-2:55 is a roll-call of people who noticed the pattern (Bacon recap, Forster, Humboldt, the hook list read again, two 1970s jokes). Nothing new on the 'why' arrives after 0:31, and the first promised payoff (dig to China) lands only at 4:09, past the playbook's 2:00. The consensus curve sheds 8.2 points in minute 2 and 5.4 in minute 3, the steepest slope after the intro; the casual viewer leaves at 2:41. Of this block, the Forster flood stretch plants nothing for later, and it holds five of the bug-finder's animation defects (S2-1 to S2-5: paper snag 1:48.0, whip hiccup 1:57.1-1:58.5, running in place 2:01.8-2:03.5, wave pop 2:04.4, vanishing water beads 2:07.7-2:10.9).
fixes.fix: Cut 99.30-131.10 s (1:39.30-2:11.10, 31.8 s), from the first frame of the Latin page to the first frame of the Humboldt portrait. This removes 'So Bacon saw the drip... That did not stop them from trying.' and all of Forster through 'Geology later asked for a refund.' The join reads '...shaped alike, side by side. / By the eighteen-forties, the most famous scientist alive was calling the tips pyramidal.' Both sides are digital silence in vo_proc.wav, and the onset of 'By' (from 131.12 s) survives. Every plant survives: 'not... mere accident' (1:07), 'Remember that' (1:24), the first JUICE CHECK stamp (1:30), 'pyramidal' (2:11), 'Hold on to him' (2:46). The word 'drip' is now coined at 2:29 before it is used. If the ~0.25-s pause sounds rushed, pad 0.25 s and freeze the last map frame for 8 frames (a one-line edl.py extension).
fixes.expected_effect: The history block drops from 120 s to 88 s; 'They line up' moves to ~3:06 and the dig-to-China payoff to ~3:38. Expect about 2 more points held from 2:11 on (AVD +1-1.5 points), and five animation defects disappear without a re-render.

fixes.problem: Frames 0-90 (0:00.0-0:03.0) show the same still globe (motion 0.10-0.35/s) while the voice says 'Spin a globe'. The white arrows into the '?' ring, which are thumbnail B's whole idea ('POINTING AT WHAT?'), only start at 0:03.3. The flat map (0:07.8-0:16) is then the longest still run of the first minute: seven names are read and all the tip pins drop together at 0:14-0:16. The 0:30 number (YouTube's Intro metric, 68% consensus) is decided here.
fixes.fix: Re-render the first 16 s with existing assets and no narration change. Enter on the globe mid-spin (about 150 degrees), easing onto the current framing by 0:02.5. Start the three tip-to-'?' arcs at about frame 10 instead of 0:03.3, so frame 1 reads as thumbnail B in motion. On the flat map, drop each tip's pin and red drip on its name (Greenland 0:07.8, Florida 0:09.2, Baja 0:10.0, Kamchatka 0:11.0) and add a slow 5% push-in over 0:07.8-0:16. Alternative from R3: open on the 0:16 flat-map drip frame for 2 s, then cut to the globe on 'South America' (0:03.9).
fixes.expected_effect: +2-4 points at 0:30. Because everything later scales from it, that is about +1-1.5 points AVD.

fixes.problem: Right after the hook's last promise, the picture hard-cuts to pure black at 0:53.10 and stays black for 1.43 s, with 'Eventually.' (0:53.12-0:54.32) said over it. It then fades up to the history map over 0:54.53-0:55.04. On a TV or phone this reads as the video ending or buffering, at the 0:30-1:00 decision point.
fixes.fix: Picture-only, timeline unchanged: keep the 0:52 four-model grid on screen through 'Eventually.' and slam the four tiles together on the word (the existing impact hit already sits there), or dim the grid to ~30% with a slow push. Crossfade to the sepia map so it is fully up on 'Bad news' (0:55.04). If any black stays, keep it to 6-8 frames. The hit itself is fine: the audio check found the voice 15-40 dB clear at 1-4 kHz.
fixes.expected_effect: +1-1.5 points at 1:00 (58% to about 59.5%).

fixes.problem: The title's answer is barely animated. The polar map holds still from 11:12.35 to 11:21.6. Its tip markers arrive only on 'Antarctica' (S7-9), and a fourth Ma counter rolls 38-176 over the already-assembled map (11:12.5-11:13.3). Then, on 'As they drifted apart, they roughly kept their orientation', the whole 180-to-0 Ma breakup runs in about 40 frames (11:21.63-11:23.03), through a double exposure: '180/178' ghosted at 11:21.7-11:21.9, and '1' over 'TODAY' at 11:22.93. No tip markers show during the move, so 'kept their orientation' can't be seen, and 'They're scars' lands on narration alone.
fixes.fix: Re-time 11:12.35-11:33.4 using the paleo-globe module from 10:32-11:12. Show a static '180' on the polar map, and draw the red tip markers and dashed lines on 'pointy ends' (~11:18.4). Cut cleanly, with no dissolve, to the 180 Ma globe on 'As they drifted' (11:21.71). Run 180 to 0 over ~6 s (11:21.7-11:27.8, ease-out), with tip-to-Antarctica tether lines from the first frame that stretch as the pieces move. Fade the counter out before 'TODAY' fades in. Land on the finished TODAY globe with dotted lines during 'still aim back to where they tore away' (11:25.6-11:29.0), and hold through 'They're scars' (11:31.87) and its 1-s pause.
fixes.expected_effect: The payoff becomes visible proof. That raises satisfaction, likes and subscriptions where viewers judge whether the title was answered, and keeps about +0.5-1 point across 11:30-13:00.

fixes.problem: 'So is the drip just a coincidence?' (14:04.77), then a summary and 'The likeliest answer: it's a snapshot...' (to 14:34.77), makes a 30-s recap at 84% of the runtime. It sits over the stillest window of the film (14:00-14:30: motion 0.72, 8 still seconds) and reads as the ending, 2.5 min before the four-continents payoff promised at 0:47 and the comment prompt at 15:30. Three closers then stack again at 15:55-16:19 ('Whichever future wins...', the Bacon callback, 'one frame of a very slow movie').
fixes.fix: Keep the verdict 14:04.77-14:19.41 with the IT'S COMPLICATED stamp, and show the 11:32 scar-lines shot under 'they're scars from a supercontinent' (14:09.8). Move 859.50-875.40 s ('And the rest of the lopsided planet?... happen to be right now' plus its polaroid; cap the 14:30.83 flash at about half brightness) into the slot of 954.93-963.03 s ('Whichever future wins... where the pieces have been'), which is dropped. 'Connecting dots.' then runs into the chapter-6 card and 'So where is the drip going?' with a ~0.45-s pause, and 'snapshot' sets up 'one frame of a very slow movie' (16:14.6), with every loop still closed. edl.py only cuts, so the move needs a small extension or a hand edit. Fallback: cut both ranges (24 s).
fixes.expected_effect: Removes the false ending and one stacked closer (net -7.8 s). Expect +1.5-2 points still watching at the 15:30 comment prompt and the end screen, and about +0.5 point AVD.

fixes.problem: Right after the best punchline ('Argentinians', 4:33.9), six numbers arrive in 53 s at 172-178 wpm, over the stillest pictures so far (7 still seconds in each of 4:30-5:00 and 5:00-5:30). The takes s035-s036 are the fastest in the film (4.82 syllables/s, 27% over the median), and the IF RANDOM grid pops on over 10 consecutive frames (4:48.0-4:48.3). This is where the average viewer starts to tire.
fixes.fix: Cut two restatements, both on digital silence. (a) 284.90-290.27 s (4:44.90-4:50.27): 'That's less than half of what you'd expect if the continents had been sprinkled at random.' plus the dot grid; '1 IN 8' carries the point, and the join lands on the puzzle globe on 'So try a puzzle.' (b) 306.45-312.10 s (5:06.45-5:12.10): 'There is no way to cut this planet in half and get a half that's mostly land.' plus the X grids; 'And it's still more than half water.' already says it. The join lands on the 89% globe on 'Now flip the globe over.' Each join keeps a ~0.4-s pause. This also removes the bug-finder's S4-8 defect (moth-eaten grids).
fixes.expected_effect: 11 s less of the densest stretch; about +0.5-1 point held from 5:00.

fixes.expected_effect: Removes the audible AI-splice glitches on the 4:17 punchline and the 9:10 death beat, and fixes the name on the chapter's payoff line. Small curve effect (+0.2-0.3 point) but real gains in perceived quality and trust.

fixes.problem: 12:55.87-12:57.0 is an empty dark-navy frame with only a teal scan line sliding down. The first tile ghosts in at 12:57.0, and the 12-tile grid is full at about 12:57.4, all under 'Now, the honest part...'. fixes.problem: At 5:45.00-5:45.03 (frames 10350-10351, the render-chunk 22/23 seam, scan ratio 12.4), the globe inside the 1875 tetrahedron drops to about half brightness in one frame, 0.3 s before 'And it wasn't a ball'. fixes.problem: The key claim 'Almost everywhere you look, land has ocean on its far side, not more land' (3:47.7-3:53.2) plays over a plain rotating globe. The antipode overlay that proves it is visible for only about 1.5 s (3:50.0-3:51.5) and is gone before 'not more land'.

fixes.problem: The four future models use one template four times. Each full-screen model snaps into its grid cell in 3-4 frames and stops dead (15:02.2, 15:11.3, 15:19.9, 15:29.3; motion 0 to 9 to 0.00), with label pops and frozen globes, during the film's slowest narration (106 wpm). (15:35.2-15:37.6), and the 'TUESDAY' calendar callback shows for only ~0.5 s (15:42.50-15:43.03), after the joke.

Cross-dissolve or whip from globe to globe on 'Two:' (15:02.5), 'Three:' (15:12.1) and 'Four:' (15:20.2), keep every globe slowly rotating, and fade the MODEL labels over 6-8 frames. Keep the grid only at 14:52 and for the comment prompt (15:29.9-15:37.5), and walk the character below the panels. Bring the calendar in on 'Just' (15:41.9), hold it ~1.5 s, and strike through 'TUESDAY' on the word. Optional (R4): show each collision with the 1:30 shake-and-stamp hit.

fixes.problem: Florida's 'limestone platform' is a flat beige trapezoid. It shoots up in 0.6 s, then sits near-still for about 9 s (13:31.9-13:41), with sea-life icons ~30 px wide on a phone. fixes.problem: Other render faults the reviewers flagged; the 5:32, 9:48 and 12:19 ones are frame-checked. 5:32.2-5:34.6: the Pacific 'water half' globe sits on an opaque, tilted black square (S4-4). 9:48.6-9:48.73: the FINGERNAILS VS TOENAILS card jerks, then the whole frame stays ~15% darker (luma 33.6 to 28.9). 10:34.43: a one-frame coastline jump on 'Cracks open'. 7:06.5-7:12: the '1918' label floats on black, and the kids pop in on single frames and snap poses at 7:11.9. 12:19.5-12:22.0: the right half of the split screen is empty for 0.5 s, and the label arrives only at 12:22.0. 6:03.87 and 6:57.93: full-white pages hard-cut to near-black (frame diff 174 and 141). 4:35.1-4:36.3: a reused 'surfacing' insert sits under 'Now flip every continent'.

Give the kids 6-8-frame pop-ins and blended poses, and parent the label to the card. Label both split-screen halves from 12:19.3, and draw Holden's 1970 arrows on 'for real, how Pangaea broke apart'. fixes.problem: All 109 takes use the default speed, so delivery stays at 3.6-4.2 syllables/s in every minute. The honest part (12:55-14:35) is six long, uniform takes (s091-s096) with no hold over 1.0 s, right where the title question is answered. 'A bent card dipped in water' (6:11.3-6:12.2) is heard as 'a bent car' in 4/4 ASR passes. R4 wants 0.5-0.9-s beats before about 12 punchlines; the audio check finds pausing mostly fine and puts the real risk in these stretches.
fixes.fix: Regenerate a few takes, keeping lengths within 0.2 s wherever the picture keys off word times. s046: 'a bent card, dipped in water'. s095: 'So is the drip just a coincidence?' as its own take at speed 0.9, with a ~1.1-s hold. Add a 0.7-1.0-s hold before 'And Africa's real southern tip' (~13:46.8). s064-s065 (the death beat): speed 0.9. s035: split before 'Only about one-eighth', with a 0.5-s pause at speed 0.92, only if 4:36-4:52 is re-rendered anyway. Accept a take only when ASR returns the right words.
fixes.expected_effect: Breaks the 'one long read' feel in the honest part and lets the key question land; +0.2-0.4 point, mostly in perceived quality.

keep: Hook copy 0:00-0:53: 'Spin a globe, and Earth looks like it's melting', the seven-name list, 'dashboard in July' (0:14.7), the myth stated at 0:24.7 and broken at 0:28.9 ('They're not. Not entirely.'), the 0:30 Gondwana flash-forward, and the three-item roadmap ending on 'Eventually.'

The Bacon loops: 'not to be attributed to mere accident' (1:07.7), paid off by 'It wasn't an accident. It was a breakup.' (16:11-16:14); and 'is there even a southern continent?... Remember that.' (1:15-1:25), paid off at 10:23-10:31.
